claims.claim: A ceremony is usually required after a successful adult British citizenship application.
claims.quote: You need to attend a citizenship ceremony if you’re 18 or over and have successfully applied to become a British citizen.
claims.note: The page requires a ceremony for successful adult applicants, subject to its stated exceptions.

claims.claim: The ceremony must be attended within 3 months of the Home Office invitation.
claims.quote: You must attend a citizenship ceremony within 3 months of receiving your invitation from the Home Office.
claims.note: The page gives the same three month deadline and trigger.

claims.claim: At the ceremony, make an oath or affirmation.
claims.quote: You’ll have to make an oath of allegiance (or an affirmation if you prefer not to swear by God) and a pledge.
claims.note: The page requires an oath or affirmation at the ceremony.

claims.claim: At the ceremony, receive a certificate of British citizenship.
claims.quote: At the end of the ceremony you’ll be presented with your certificate of British citizenship and a welcome pack.
claims.note: The page says the certificate is presented at the end.

claims.claim: Attendance is optional under the Windrush scheme.
claims.quote: If you become a British citizen under the Windrush scheme you can choose if you want to attend a citizenship ceremony.
claims.note: The page makes attendance a choice for this group.

claims.claim: Adults aged 18 or over who successfully apply for British citizenship usually need to attend a ceremony.

claims.note: The page states this requirement, with a Windrush choice elsewhere.

claims.claim: Children under 18 who applied with their parents may attend a parent’s ceremony.
claims.quote: Children under 18 who have applied with their parents may attend a ceremony with other members of the family, to collect their certificate.
claims.note: The guidance permits children who applied with their parents to attend the family ceremony.
